record.what_it_does: Slack is a business messaging platform, and its Web API lets apps read, write, and manage messages, channels, users, files, and other workspace data on a user's or bot's behalf.
record.auth_notes: Slack apps are installed via OAuth v2 (authorization code flow) to obtain bot (xoxb) or user (xoxp) bearer tokens, which are then sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every Web API call. There is also a dedicated `oauth.v2.user.access` flow built specifically for MCP-client authorization.
record.access_notes: Any developer can create an app for free at api.slack.com/apps, install it to their own workspace instantly, and start calling the Web API with no cost and no approval. Public distribution to other workspaces via OAuth is also self-serve and doesn't require review; only submitting the app for listing in the Slack Marketplace (commercial directory) requires a manual vendor review, and the official MCP server further restricts non-internal use to apps published in the Marketplace.
record.main_blocker: Multi-tenant/commercial distribution and MCP access require Slack Marketplace review; unlisted apps are prohibited from using the official MCP server
